 Add Wire: Use conductive eyebolt at antenna top to install wires for an inverted "L" or a "T" to enhance low frequency coverage.

 Low SWR: No tuner is needed for 80 / 75 / 60 / 40 / 17 Meters, because radiator length is fixed at 31. Operation on 30 / 20 / 15 / 12 / 10 / 6M requires an ATU.

text:
The Band Optimized Log Periodic Dipole Array (BOLPA) is the brain child of Justin Johnson G0KSC and is the combination of multiple 3 element monoband Log Periodic Arrays on one boom. It has long been known that the Log Periodic can provide directional performance over a very wide range. Some years ago, Justin G0KSC decided to experiment with narrow-band Log Periodic Arrays to ascertain if additional performance (in terms of Front to Back ratio (F/B) and forward (Gain) could be achieved. Justin established that with just 3 tightly packed elements, excellent F/B and gain could be achieved across the whole of the amateur bands within a very short boom length. At the same time it can deliver a 50 Ohm feed point impedance rather than the more traditional 200 Ohm. To give an example of size, one of these 3 element monoband Log Periodic Arrays for 20 Meters would sit on a boom a little over 6 in length. 
 The BOLPA is a combination of 3 element monoband Log Periodic Arrays upon the same boom. The BOLPA 13 being 3 elements on 20m, 15m, 10m and 6m. In this antenna, 12 Meters is a bonus band, it is delivered between the 3 elements for 15 Meters and the 3 elements for 10 Meters almost by accident. A small amount of optimization of the spacing between the 15 Meter 3 element cell and that of the 10 meter cell finalized the performance. With 17 Meters, a little more work was needed. The 20 Meter, 3 element cell was shifted back along the boom. This allows for an additional single element to be placed between the 20 Meter 3 element cell and the 15 Meter 3 element cell. Only the width of this single 17 Meter element and the position of the 20 Meter cell and 15 Meter cell (along the boom) were optimized to achieve excellent performance.   
The addition of the 17 Meter band element did more than just provide excellent performance on 17 Meters. The same applied on 15 Meters where the single 17 Meter element was now able to be used as a reflector type function for 15 Meters. This allowed all 3 of the elements in the 15 Meter cell to be optimized for maximum gain and F/B resulting once more in another band with 4 active elements.

name: VEC-1862, ANTENNA, 6M YAGI
text:
A directional antenna is essential for long distance VHF communication. By focusing transmitter power onto the horizon in a single direction, vectronics three element 6 Meter Yagi quadruples your ERP (effective radiated power) over a half-wave dipole. 
The same benefit applies when receiving -- sensitivity toward the front of the antenna is improved by 6 dB over a dipole, while unwanted noise and interference from other directions are rejected. 
The VEC-1862s main lobe (area of maximum sensitivity) is 70 to 80 degrees wide. This means you can converse with several stations in one general direction without having to constantly reposition your rotator for maximum signal. 
Two VEC-1862s can be stacked to double your transmitter ERP and your received signal over a single VEC-1862. It also doubles your received signal. Stacked antennas also have greater capture area, which can improve reception even more. 
The VEC-1862 weighs just 2 pounds and has a boom length of 6 feet. It is designed for installation with readily available TV mast, mounts and hardware. 
The driven element uses Vectronics NoTuneHairpin impedance matching system, and element are cut to exact length at the factory. No further tuning is needed for 50 MHz SSB coverage. 
Because of its compact size, lightweight construction, and easy-to-remove elements, the VEC-1862 is also an excellent choice for 6 - Meter portable or rover operation. 
VEC-1862 handles 300 watts PEP SSB and can be mounted horizontally or vertically. A current balun decouples the 50 Ohm feedline from the antenna. It has 6 dBD of forward gain and backlobe attenuation of 18 dB.

name: CHA SKYLOOP 40
text:
CHA SKYLOOP 40 
Full-Wave Loop Performance in a Practical 40-Meter Footprint 
The CHA SKYLOOP 40 is a full-size horizontal loop antenna engineered for operators who want excellent HF performance, quiet reception, broad radiation coverage, and dependable multiband operation without the enormous installation area required by larger full-wave loops. 
Constructed from 141 feet of rugged 16-gauge wire , the antenna provides operation across the entire 40- and 20-meter amateur bands without an antenna tuner when properly installed and adjusted. When used with a suitable antenna tuner, it also supports the 17-, 15-, 12-, and 10-meter bands , creating a highly versatile six-band antenna system for home stations, base camps, emergency communications, and shortwave listening. 
An integral broadband 2.5:1 matching transformer provides the impedance transformation required to connect the loop to a standard 50-ohm coaxial feed line. The matching unit is equipped with an SO-239 connector , secure wing-nut wire terminals, an integrated support eyebolt, strain-relief hardware, and a ground connection. 
Designed for Real-World Installations 
When installed as a square, each side of the CHA SKYLOOP 40 is approximately 35¼ feet long . However, a perfect square is not required. Individual sides may be made longer or shorter to accommodate available trees, masts, fence posts, building attachment points, or other safe supports, provided the total loop length remains approximately 141 feet. 
This flexibility makes the CHA SKYLOOP 40 an excellent choice for: 
Home and base stations 
Smaller properties where a larger loop will not fit 
HOA-conscious and visually discreet installations 
Emergency and disaster communications 
Base-camp and semi-permanent field stations 
Regional and long-distance HF communications 
Near-Vertical Incidence Skywave communications 
Shortwave and general-coverage listening 
The lowest recommended optimal installation height is approximately 30 feet , although the antenna can still provide excellent results when installed lower. Raising the loop generally improves efficiency and supports broader regional and long-distance communication. A lower horizontal installation emphasizes the high-angle radiation useful for NVIS communications , particularly on 40 meters. 
Actual performance will vary with installation height, loop shape, ground conductivity, surrounding objects, terrain, feed-line routing, propagation conditions, and station configuration.

name: QRP Reel Antenna
text:
This is a hand made Reel Antenna with a built in transformer. A full wire antenna on a reel all while being smaller than most QRP radios! This is incredible for POTA, SOTA and other portable/field operations. Setup in any end fed configuration you like. 
 The modular version has the transformer in a small cylindrical cover which can nest into the spool (instead of the transformer built into the winder itself.) In the modular version, pull out the transformer, attached to the radio/coax/atu and then walk out the antenna radiator...The radiator end is terminated with a loop that hooks onto the spool internal hooks. As there is no permanent attachment of the radiating wire to the spool, simply insert the loop end of the wire into the spool and rotate the handle to catch the loop on one of the 4 internal hooks. You can wind in either direction! 
Wire is Polystealth 26awg for ultimate portability, silky smoothness and unmatched durability and performance per foot! 
Super lightweight Spool! 
31' Modular BNC-F 2.5oz / 71g

 All parts are printed in ASA and PETG and can handle the elements but is not intended for long term or permanent outside installation.

Wire length if included in selection is cut to length and terminated with banana connectors at the transformer and loops at the opposite ends.
